A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Trust Region alignment work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original toy-MDP simulations and Pythia/Llama3 experiments, including preference comparisons, hyperparameter ablations, and overoptimization analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and adds downstream-task, jailbreak, and computational-overhead results. Its attribution of certain baseline scores to Meng et al. does not change the presence of original results.

M1.justification: The DPO, IPO, and KTO objectives and their soft and periodic hard reference-update procedures remain unchanged. The additional derivation and implementation explanations do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds MixEval coverage of knowledge, comprehension, commonsense, and mathematical tasks, including MMLU, GPQA, HellaSwag, MATH, and GSM8K. Appendix G adds adversarial scenarios using GPTFuzz questions and AdvBench prompts. Existing training datasets and preference benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged: SFT and the relevant DPO, IPO, and KTO baselines remain. The new evaluations extend these comparisons; GPTFuzz and ReNeLLM are attack procedures, not additional alignment baselines. Replacing baseline scores does not change method membership.

E3.justification: v4 introduces downstream evaluation and a detailed jailbreak protocol with specified attack/evaluator models, search limits, and top-one, top-five, and overall attack-success metrics. Appendix D.3 adds a one-epoch UltraFeedback runtime comparison. Previously reported training settings, splits, and preference-evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds explicit adversarial robustness tests asking whether alignment gains confer jailbreak resistance. Appendix D.3 adds an analysis of reference-update computational overhead. Existing hyperparameter, probability-mass, human-centric, diversity, response-length, and generation-example analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100-seed toy experiments, standard deviations, benchmark confidence intervals, Fisher tests, and probability-of-improvement analyses. v4 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased run count; changed uncertainty values accompany revised results.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 7 replace baseline values: for example, Llama3-Base Arena-Hard DPO changes from 10.5 to 15.9 and IPO from 8.9 to 17.8, with v4 attributing baselines to Meng et al. TR table scores remain unchanged. Figure 1 corrects soft TR-KTO's Arena-Hard value from 15.3 to 14.9, already reported in v3's Table 2. Added results include MixEval scores, uniformly 100% ReNeLLM attack success, and 2.87–7.44% training-time overhead.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds the IPO gradient and Hessian derivation, including the residual definition and Hessian decomposition in Equations 12–15. This extends the existing curvature analysis; the DPO derivation and alignment objectives are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction revises headline DPO/IPO/KTO gains from 10.8/10.5/5.6 to 9.5/15.1/2.3 points. The new numbers match AlpacaEval length-controlled gaps, although the text still references Figure 1b, which shows Arena-Hard. The central claims about reference updates and reduced overoptimization remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds interpretations of task-dependent capability gains and losses. Appendix G explicitly limits applicability: reduced overoptimization does not confer jailbreak robustness. Section 3.1 and Appendix A extend the curvature explanation to IPO while newly acknowledging that KTO support remains empirical.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies 50 SFT epochs, 200 preference-training epochs, and the toy ID/OOD partition; these are disclosures, not established experimental changes. v4 also documents reference-model memory requirements, relative runtime overhead, jailbreak tooling and settings, and Table 2 baseline provenance. Existing hardware and hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for MixEval and its constituent benchmarks, EasyJailbreak, GPTFuzz, ReNeLLM, and AdvBench. These support the expanded evaluation; Section 2's positioning relative to RLHF, offline alignment, and Nash-based methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 condenses introductory exposition and part of Section 4.2, subdivides Appendix A, and adds efficiency and evaluation sections with corresponding appendix renumbering. Headers and affiliation change to ICLR 2025 and T-Tech. Most existing prose and the main narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds two MixEval tables and a jailbreak table, redraws Figure 1 with revised bars, labels, and Arena-Hard axis range, and reflows existing material. Figures 2–19 retain their graphics. The new knowledge-results table inadvertently carries both Table 8 and Table 9 captions.

improvement.justification: The added capability and jailbreak evaluations better delimit the unchanged method's benefits, while runtime and toy-training disclosures improve practical assessment. Reporting problems limit these gains: Section 4.3 retains a KTO interpretation contradicted by revised Table 2, and Table 11 reports 99% top-one but 98% top-five attack success for soft TR-DPO. The new IPO derivation also does not establish its asserted overall curvature decrease. The useful expansion therefore provides a modest overall improvement.
